questions.stem: Cell to cell transfer using actin is feature of which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Listeria monocytogenes

Microbiological Characteristics: Listeria Monocytogenes

  • Short, gram-positive, non-spore-forming rod.
  • Catalase positive.
  • Tumbling end-over-end motility at 22-28°C, distinguishing it from diphtheroids.
  • Actin-based motility observed in Listeria monocytogenes.
  • Actin A serves as a virulence factor facilitating cell-to-cell spread.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 27 Edition, Page No.197

questions.stem: An 18-day old neonate with poor feeding and ill-being was taken to a doctor who observed neck rigidity with Kernig sign and nuchal rigidity. The mother gave a history of genital lesions which was resolved spontaneously, the child showed vesicular lesions with multinucleated giant cells on smear from the vesicle Causative agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
VZV
  • The given description is of Tzanck cells seen in Tzanck smear in c/o varicella infection.
  • The child is most likely suffering from encephalitis due to congenital varicella syndrome.
  • The correct causative agent is indeed A. VZV (Varicella-Zoster Virus), as supported by the characteristic clinical presentation and laboratory findings, including multinucleated giant cells in Tzanck smear.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology. 27th Edition, Page No. 469

questions.stem: Vibrio Cholera affects which part of the extracellular component of tight junction?
questions.solutionHtml:
Occludin
  • The zona occludens toxins of v.cholerae disrupts the tight junctions between the enterocytes. i.e., the zona occludens, particularly the occludin component of the tight junction.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 254

questions.stem: Which virus would require reverse transcriptase before PCR?
questions.solutionHtml:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
  • Reverse transcriptase is an enzyme that converts ssRNA  into dsDNA.
  • Among the given options, RSV has an RNA genome, whereas the rest of the viruses have a DNA genome.
  • Hence, RSV would require reverse transcriptase before undergoing PCR

Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) because RSV has an RNA genome, and a reverse transcriptase is required to convert its single-stranded RNA into double-stranded DNA for PCR amplification.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 587

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by the vector shown in the image below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Orientia
  • The given image is of hard tick – ixodid tick.
  • It is responsible for a common vector borne disease – lyme disease caused by borrelia burgdorferi.
  • The bacteria is transmitted from rodents/deer to humans with an ixodid tick as a vector.

questions.stem: Which of the following helps the Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) to penetrate into the host cell?
questions.solutionHtml:
gp120
  • Entry of the virus requires gp120.
  • CD4 receptors bind to Gp120 & results in conformational change.


Essentials of Medical Microbiology Apurba S Sastry 3rd Edition, Chapter 21 Page No. 326

questions.stem: HPV vaccine contains which of the following components?
questions.solutionHtml:
L1
  • Gardasil, the HPV vaccine, is a subunit vaccine containing recombinant L1 protein.
  • L1 protein forms virus-like particles that induce a strong immune response.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 634

questions.stem: An Immunocompromised individual with a white lesion on the side of the tongue which does not wipe off, most likely cause is?
questions.solutionHtml:
EBV
  • The white lesion on the side of the tongue that does not wipe off is indicative of leukoplakia.
  • EBV is the cause of oral hairy leukoplakia, especially in immunocompromised individuals like those with HIV.
  • In summary, The most likely cause of an immunocompromised individual with a non-wipeable white lesion on the side of the tongue is A. EBV (Epstein-Barr Virus), specifically associated with oral hairy leukoplakia.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 476

questions.stemHtml: A person recently recovered from Covid-19 who was treated with steroids. After 3 weeks, he complains of blood tinged nasal discharge. Swab collected and the following image is seen on microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mucor

Clinical Scenario:

  • Patient History: Recently recovered from Covid-19, treated with steroids.
  • Symptoms: Blood-tinged nasal discharge after 3 weeks.
  • Diagnosis: As per the given clinical history, the diagnosis is rhino cerebral mucormycosis caused by mucor.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 691

questions.stemHtml: A farmer from Tamil Nadu presents with fever, body ache, and cough for 3 days. Lab studies showed thrombocytopenia. On examination, a black lesion is present as in the picture below. IgM scrub typhus positive. What drug will be used in the management?
questions.solutionHtml:
Doxycycline + Azithromycin
  • Doxycycline is the drug of choice for scrub typhus & azithromycin is given to prevent secondary bacterial infection.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 343

questions.stem: A patient with a 3-day history of high grade fever, which of the following cannot help in the diagnosis of dengue?
questions.solutionHtml:
IgM ELISA
  • IgM ELISA has good sensitivity for diagnosis only after 7 days of illness.
  • All other options helps in the diagnosis of dengue with a 3 day history.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 553

questions.stem: Which of the following is a biosafety level- 3 infection ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Extensively drug- resistant (XDR)-TB

To avoid laboratory acquired infections, BSL3 practices are required especially when working with live cultures.




Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 272

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl presented with fever and retro-orbital pain for 2 days. The tourniquet test and NS1 antigen test were positive. Which of the following features is considered a criterion for the severe form of this disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
AST/ALT > 1000
  • Elevated levels of AST (aspartate aminotransferase) and ALT (alanine aminotransferase) exceeding 1000 units per liter of serum are considered a criterion for severe dengue.
  • This elevation indicates liver involvement and potential liver damage, which can be observed in severe cases of dengue fever.


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 3715

questions.stemHtml: The toxin produced by which of the following organisms acts by the mechanism shown in the image below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Corynebacterium diphtheriae

The above given image shows the function of Fragment A of Diptheria Toxin.

  • Fragment A inhibits polypeptide chain elongation—provided nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) is present—by inactivating the elongation factor EF-2.
  • This factor is required for translocation of polypeptidyl-transfer RNA from the acceptor to the donor site on the eukaryotic ribosome.
  • Toxin Fragment A inactivates EF-2 by catalyzing a reaction that yields free nicotinamide plus an inactive adenosine diphosphate-ribose-EF-2 complex (ADP-ribosylation).
  • It is assumed that the abrupt arrest of protein synthesis is responsible for the necrotizing and neurotoxic effects of diphtheria toxin


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 193

questions.stem: A patient hailing from an area infested with mosquitoes presents with fever, chills, and myalgias. WBC count was 4000 cells/cu.mm, RBC was normal, and platelets were 90000 cells/cu.mm. He also had a maculopapular rash. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dengue

Dengue:

  • Clinical Presentation: Fever, chills, myalgias, and maculopapular rash are characteristic features of dengue.
  • Laboratory Findings: Low WBC count (4000 cells/cu.mm) and low platelet count (90000 cells/cu.mm) are consistent with dengue.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 552

questions.stemHtml: A farmer presented with fever and a skin lesion as shown in the image below. Blood investigation revealed creatinine levels of 1.4 mg/dl and platelet levels of 86,000 cells/ mm3. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Scrub typhus

Scrub Typhus:

  • Clinical Presentation: Skin lesion (eschar) is a characteristic feature of scrub typhus.
  • Blood Investigations: Can lead to complications like renal impairment (elevated creatinine) and thrombocytopenia (low platelet levels).


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 27th Edition, Page Number: 343
